per_rubric.criteria: Accepts the insertion of a preamble identifying the parties to the agreement.
per_rubric.justification: The preamble identifying the parties at p-003 remains as an untouched tracked insertion with no contradicting change.

per_rubric.criteria: Accepts in Section 2.4 the insertion of "as mutually agreed to by the parties.
per_rubric.justification: The ', as mutually agreed to by the parties' insertion in Basic Service (p-013, §2.4) is left intact with no strike-through.

per_rubric.criteria: Rejects in Section 2 the insertion of the definition of "Customer Data" in its entirety.
per_rubric.justification: The Customer Data definition at p-018 (§2.8) remains as an insertion and is not struck or rejected.

per_rubric.criteria: Accepts in Section 2.10 the insertion of "is executed by both Parties."
per_rubric.justification: The 'executed by both Parties' language in the Effective Date definition (p-021, §2.10) is retained as accepted insertions.

per_rubric.criteria: Accepts in Section 2 the deletion of the definition of "Protected Health Information" in its entirety.
per_rubric.justification: The Protected Health Information definition (p-026) remains tracked-deleted with no reinsertion, so the deletion is accepted.

per_rubric.criteria: Rejects in Section 5.2 the deletion of "worldwide".
per_rubric.justification: In §5.2 (p-041), 'worldwide, royalty-free,' remains struck through; the deletion was not rejected.

per_rubric.criteria: Rejects in Section 6.1  insertion of ", and, for the avoidance of doubt, Customer shall have no obligation for payment of any invoice that is submitted by AgentCo more than ninety (90) days after the date the Service was provided."
per_rubric.justification: The ninety-day no-payment insertion in §6.1 (p-043) remains as untracked-rejection-free insertion, not struck.

per_rubric.criteria: Rejects in Section  6.3 the deletion of "Past-due undisputed amounts may bear a finance charge on the unpaid balance, accruing daily and compounding monthly, at the prevailing Federal Funds Rate (floored at zero) plus 1.5% per annum."
per_rubric.justification: The finance-charge sentence in §6.3 (p-045) remains struck through; the deletion was not rejected.

per_rubric.criteria: Accepts in Section 6.3 the insertion of "and provided Customer with at least fifteen (15) business days to cure any outstanding past due amount(s)."
per_rubric.justification: The fifteen-business-day cure language in §6.3 (p-045) is left as an intact insertion with no contradicting change.

per_rubric.criteria: Rejects in Section 6.3 the deletion of "In any billing dispute, all undisputed amounts must be paid in full when due."
per_rubric.justification: The billing-dispute sentence in §6.3 (p-045) remains struck through; the deletion was not rejected.

per_rubric.criteria: Replaces in Section 7.1 the ten day notice period for LargeCo to terminate for convenience with thirty days notice.
per_rubric.justification: §7.1 (p-047) strikes 'ten (10) days' notice' and inserts 'thirty (30) days' prior written notice' for Customer termination.

per_rubric.criteria: Rejects in Section 7.4 the deletion of "and unpaid".
per_rubric.justification: In §7.4 (p-051), 'and unpaid' remains struck through; the deletion was accepted rather than rejected.

per_rubric.criteria: Rejects in Section 8.1 the insertion of "or (ii) a breach by AgentCo of any term of this Agreement,".
per_rubric.justification: §8.1 contains no tracked strike of the breach-of-agreement insertion; the rejection is only implied by its absence and the comment.

per_rubric.criteria: Rejects in Section 8.1 the replacement of "finally awarded" with "in the defense".
per_rubric.justification: §8.1 shows no tracked change against the 'in the defense' replacement; 'finally awarded' stands only by absence of an edit.

per_rubric.criteria: Rejects in Section 10.2 the insertion of ", a party’s confidentiality obligations under Section 11.5, AgentCo’s breach of data security,".
per_rubric.justification: §10.2 (p-062) tracked-deletes the 11.5 confidentiality, AgentCo data-security, and breach-of-data-security insertion language, rejecting it.
